title: Sordim: separating AI art approval from Unity integration in a co-op survival RPG
author: Common_Rush8322
selftext:
I am developing Sordim at Lippe Studios in Brazil: a co-op survival RPG for up to eight players, coming to Steam on PC.



I split the AI workflow between Claude for Unity code and integration, and ChatGPT for visual assets. I review previews before approving a final asset. Approved art stays in a staging folder, and Claude handles importing it into Unity. Each approval applies to the specific visual revision I saw.



The practical constraint is keeping those steps separate: generation, visual approval, then integration. Written handoffs track the filenames and what has been approved, so a newer generated revision does not silently replace the approved one.



Sordim cinematic: [https://youtu.be/cRInw1\_fFuU](https://youtu.be/cRInw1_fFuU)



How do you track approved visual revisions when different assistants handle code and art? I would like to compare approaches with other developers here.



AI disclosure: Claude assists with code, ChatGPT with visual assets and this post. I direct the project and approve the visuals.
